en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Bhūtagāmavagga 16.
The Training Rule on Intrusion.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were reserving superior lodgings, while the elder monks were vacating them.
Then it occurred to the group-of-six monks:
"By what means might we spend the rains retreat right here?"
Then the group-of-six monks intruded upon the elder monks and made their beds down, thinking, "Whoever finds it cramped shall depart.
Those monks who were of few desires... [as before] ... complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“How indeed can the monks of the group of six take up lodgings by encroaching upon the senior monks?
Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One. … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that you take up lodgings by encroaching upon the senior monks?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:

“… How can you, foolish men, lie down in the presence of the elder bhikkhus? This is not suitable for you, foolish men! … [as before] … “How indeed, foolish men, could you lie down in the presence of the elder bhikkhus?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘Whatever monk, knowing that another monk has already entered first, should intrude and make his bed in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha—’”
“Whoever has a crowded situation shall depart”—making this very condition and no other, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whoever, moreover,” means whoever of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Belonging to the Saṅgha" means a dwelling (vihāra).
It has been given to the Saṅgha and relinquished to it.
"Knows" means:
he knows that [the person] is senior, he knows that [the person] is ill, and he knows that it has been given by the Saṅgha.
"Anupakhajja" means having entered.
"Seyyaṃ kappeyya" means [one] would lie down.
If, within the vicinity of a bed or a chair as one enters or exits, one spreads out a sleeping mat oneself or has one spread out, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If one sits down or lies down upon it, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
This is done with no other purpose than for this very reason.
There is no other condition for making one's bed encroaching upon another.
If one makes one's bed encroaching upon what belongs to the Saṅgha while perceiving it as belonging to the Saṅgha, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one makes one's bed encroaching upon what belongs to the Saṅgha while being doubtful about it, there is an offense of expiation.
If one spreads out a bed or has one spread out, occupying a sleeping place belonging to the Saṅgha while perceiving it as belonging to an individual, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, setting aside the immediate vicinity of a bed or a chair, one spreads out a bed or has one spread out, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one sits down or lies down [on it], there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If one spreads out a bed, or causes one to be spread out, in the vicinity of a monastery, or in a hall for attendance, or in a pavilion, or at the foot of a tree, or in the open air, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If one sits down on it or lies down on it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it belongs to an individual and one perceives it as belonging to the Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is for an individual and he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is for an individual and he perceives it as being for an individual, yet it belongs to another individual, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is for one's own individual use, there is no offense.
There is no offense if he enters while ill,
or if he enters because he is oppressed by cold or heat.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The sixth training rule concerning sitting down by pushing in is finished.
